plan.title: Colon treated vs control DE (RSEM counts, n=6/6)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level matrix of RSEM expected counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv, gene symbols in column 1) with metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, human colon. The research question is simply which genes differ between treated and control, so the plan stops at the differential expression result and its diagnostics — no enrichment, no downstream translational steps, since none were asked for.

Two data facts drive the method choices. First, the counts are RSEM expected counts and are therefore non-integer, and the per-sample genes.results files carrying the effective lengths were NOT delivered. The tximport type='rsem' route, which would pass the effective lengths into the model as an offset, is therefore not executable on these inputs. T1S2 must round the expected counts to integers for DESeq2/edgeR and state explicitly in its output that the length offset is missing, that gene-level fold changes are consequently not corrected for any between-sample shift in effective length, and that the per-sample genes.results files would remove this caveat. It must not fabricate lengths and must not use a TPM column. Second, sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median. It is kept through QC and inspected on the PCA and the distance heatmap rather than deleted; median-of-ratios size factors already account for depth, so depth alone is not grounds for removal. T1S1 reports its library size and detected-gene count beside the others and states whether it also behaves as an expression outlier; only a stated non-depth reason would justify exclusion, and any such decision is reported, not silent.

T1S2 fits ~condition with control set explicitly as the reference level, contrast (condition, treated, control), a minimal pre-filter of >=10 counts in >=6 samples, the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and inspects the raw p-value histogram before trusting the adjustment. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts, so the flagged genes are counted and reported separately from genes dropped by the independent filter. T1S3 runs edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same rounded matrix as an independent second method and reports the intersection as the high-confidence set — appropriate here because 6 replicates per group sits at the low end where the two tools diverge on low-count genes, and because the missing length offset makes a single-tool result worth cross-checking. T1S4 assembles the report: MA and dispersion diagnostics, the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC and lfcSE with ranking on the shrunken value, the method overlap, and a full reproducibility record. No reference data beyond the input files is required by any step.
